correctness.rationale: The source tight right-hand side is reconstructed exactly. At the uniform point its doubled slack simplifies to s(d-s)+b(s+u-1), while the intrinsic subset-normal squared norm is s(d-s)/d. This gives the exact shell formula. The correction is nonnegative and the permutahedral baseline is minimized only at cardinalities one and d-1. Singleton tight inequalities give a matching all-center radius upper bound when summed, and equality forces every center coordinate to be equal, proving uniqueness.

value.rationale: Higher Hochschild polytopes are the genuinely multi-light members of a recent family with combinatorics and lattice behavior that change beyond the one-light case. The theorem gives a closed metric law for every tight subset hyperplane, not merely an isolated radius. It explains quantitatively why all higher members retain the classical permutahedral inradius: every nonterminal selected shade coordinate contributes an explicit outward shell penalty.
